title: In conversation with Sergey Stavisky
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02443-5As part of our special issue on Neurotechnology, we spoke with Sergey Stavisky, Associate Professor at the University of California, Davis, about the breakthroughs that have transformed speech neuroprostheses from proof-of-concept demonstrations into practical communication systems. He reflects on the scientific surprises, engineering challenges and ethical questions that are shaping the future of neural interfaces.

title: In conversation with Miguel Nicolelis
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02467-xAs part of our special issue on neurotechnology, we spoke with Miguel Nicolelis, Professor Emeritus at Duke University and founder of the Edmond and Lily Safra International Neuroscience Institute, about the bold ideas that have defined his career, from helping to pioneer brain–machine interfaces to establishing a neuroscience institute in northeastern Brazil with the goal of driving social transformation. He considers the scientific discoveries, technological hurdles and ethical questions that continue to shape the future of neural interfaces and neurorehabilitation.

title: In conversation with Richard Andersen
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02450-6As part of our special issue on neurotechnology, we spoke with Richard Andersen, James G. Boswell Professor of Neuroscience at Caltech, about the discoveries that helped to establish the posterior parietal cortex as a key hub for intention and action planning. He looks back on decades of discoveries in the posterior parietal cortex and discusses how advances in neural recording, decoding and computation are reshaping our understanding of cognition.

title: In conversation with Edward Chang
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02453-3As part of our special issue on neurotechnology, we spoke with Edward Chang, Margaret Liu Collins and Edward B. Collins distinguished Professor and Chair of neurosurgery at the University of California, San Francisco, about the evolution of speech brain–computer interfaces (BCIs). He discusses how advances in AI are accelerating the translation of BCIs into the clinic, the challenge of restoring natural communication, and why large-scale neural datasets may ultimately help build computational models of the human brain.

title: In conversation with Jennifer Collinger
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02451-5As part of our special issue on neurotechnology, we spoke with Jennifer Collinger, Professor at the University of Pittsburgh, about how sensory feedback is reshaping brain–computer interfaces, the surprising stability of neural representations after spinal cord injury, and the scientific and engineering challenges of building truly bidirectional neuroprosthetic systems that restore movement and touch.
